questions.question: In the question, one statement is given followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly know facts. You have to decide which of the conclusion, if any, follow from the given statements. Statement: “Auto-rickshaw fares in Delhi will soon be hiked by over 39%”. Conclusion: I. Auto-rickshaw rides will now become more expensive for people. II. People will now use auto-rickshaws only for short distances.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question, one statement is given followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly know facts. You have to decide which of the conclusion, if any, follow from the given statements.

Statement: “Auto-rickshaw fares in Delhi will soon be hiked by over 39%”.

Conclusion:

I. Auto-rickshaw rides will now become more expensive for people.

II. People will now use auto-rickshaws only for short distances.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: a

Conclusion I: Auto-rickshaw rides will now become more expensive for people.

This conclusion directly follows from the statement, as a hike of over 39% in fares will naturally make auto-rickshaw rides more costly. Hence, Conclusion I is valid.

Conclusion II: People will now use auto-rickshaws only for short distances.

This conclusion does not necessarily follow from the statement. While increased fares might make people reconsider using auto-rickshaws, it does not imply they will exclusively use them for short distances. Other factors, such as convenience or alternatives, might influence their decision. Hence, Conclusion II is not valid.
